evidence.experimental_conditions: 12% (8280 µg/cm²) in petrolatum, occlusion on forearm, five alternate-day 48 h induction periods, pre-treatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate for 24 h, challenge patches for 48-72 h, panel of 25 patients
evidence.support_text: A human maximization test according to Kligman (1966) and Kligman and Epstein (1975) was conducted with 12% (8280 µg/cm²) 2-phenylpropyl acetate in petrolatum on a panel of 25 patients. Challenge patches were applied under occlusion to fresh sites for 48 or 72 h. No sensitization reactions were observed, indicating a negative outcome for skin sensitization in this human test.

evidence.support_text: In the human maximization test with HEQ at 15% w/v in distilled water, no allergic inflammatory reactions were observed in any of the 25 volunteers during challenge, and a second provocative challenge on three individuals with additional SLS pretreatment also yielded no allergic reactions. evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% (1380 µg/cm²) phenethyl isobutyrate in petrolatum; 25 healthy male patients; occlusive application to forearm for five alternate-day 48 h periods; pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS for 24 h under occlusion; 10-day rest; challenge patches on back for 48 h occlusion with 1 h pretreatment with 10% SLS; evaluation at 48 and 72 h.
evidence.support_text: A human maximization test according to Kligman with 2% (1380 µg/cm²) phenethyl isobutyrate in petrolatum on 25 healthy male patients resulted in no sensitization reactions observed.

evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test (n=25), isobutyl benzoate at 2% in petrolatum was applied to the volar surface on 5 alternate days after pretreatment with 5% SLS. At challenge, no sensitization was observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20% Ethyl Ricinoleate in petrolatum; 32 healthy male volunteers; 5 alternate-day 48-h induction applications under occlusion after 24-h pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate; 10-14 day rest; challenge patches applied to new sites for 48 h; challenge preceded by 30-min applications of 2% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate on left side; petrolatum control
evidence.support_text: The skin sensitization potential of 20% Ethyl Ricinoleate in petrolatum was evaluated using 32 healthy male volunteers in the maximization test. evidence.experimental_conditions: 27 human subjects; induction: 10% isophytol in petrolatum under occlusion to forearms, 5 alternate-day 48h periods, preceded by 24h occlusive 5% aqueous SLS; 10-day rest; challenge: 48h occlusion to fresh sites, preceded by 30 min 10% SLS under occlusion on left side, no SLS on right side; evaluated at patch removal and 24h later.
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization study with 27 subjects, there was no evidence of contact sensitization to 10% isophytol in petrolatum under the described occlusive induction and challenge protocol (RIFM, 1981).

evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test on 21 patients, 3% (2070 µg/cm²) 2,4-dimethylbenzyl acetate in petrolatum was applied under occlusion with sodium lauryl sulfate pretreatment during induction (five alternate day 48 h periods) and challenged similarly. There was no reaction in any subject.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% (1260 µg/cm²) ethyl phenyl carbinyl acetate in petrolatum; occlusion on forearm or back; five alternate-day 48 h induction periods; pre-treatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) under occlusion; 10–14 day rest; challenge patches under occlusion for 48 h with 30 min SLS pre-treatment; reactions evaluated at patch removal, 48 h, and 72 h.
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test according to Kligman (1966) and Kligman and Epstein (1975) with 4% (1260 µg/cm²) ethyl phenyl carbinyl acetate in petrolatum on 27 subjects, application under occlusion to forearms or backs for five alternate-day 48 h periods with pre-treatment by 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate, followed by a 10–14 day rest and challenge patches under occlusion for 48 h with 30 min SLS pre-treatment, no reactions (0/27) were noted (RIFM, 1982b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% (2760 µg/cm²) anisyl formate in petrolatum; application under occlusion to forearm for 5 alternate-day 48-h periods; pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) for 24 h; challenge after 10–14 day rest period on back for 48 h occlusion; challenge site pretreated with 5% SLS for 30 min; evaluation at 48 and 72 h
evidence.support_text: A maximization test with 4% (2760 µg/cm²) anisyl formate in petrolatum on 22 healthy male patients, using occlusion with SLS pretreatment, resulted in no sensitization reactions observed at the challenge site (RIFM, 1975b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% (2760 µg/cm²) benzyl butyrate in petrolatum; occlusion to forearms; five alternate day 48 h induction periods; pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) for 24 h; 10 day rest; challenge on back for 48 h with 1 h pretreatment of 10% SLS; evaluation at 48 and 72 h.
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test (Kligman, 1966; Kligman and Epstein, 1975), 4% (2760 µg/cm²) benzyl butyrate in petrolatum was applied under occlusion to the forearms of 25 healthy male patients for five alternate day 48 h periods, with pretreatment by 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS). After a 10 day rest, challenge patches were applied to fresh sites on the back with 1 h pretreatment of 10% SLS, and evaluated at 48 and 72 h. No sensitization reactions were observed (RIFM, 1973a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% (2760 µg/cm²) benzyl propionate in petrolatum; application under occlusion to forearms for five alternate-day 48 h periods; pretreatment for 24 h with 5% aqueous SLS under occlusion; 10-day rest; challenge patches on back for 48 h under occlusion with 1 h pretreatment with 10% SLS; evaluation at 48 and 72 h
evidence.support_text: A maximization test was carried out with 4% (2760 µg/cm²) benzyl propionate in petrolatum on 25 healthy male patients. Following the induction and challenge protocol, no sensitization reactions were observed (RIFM, 1973b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% 1,1-dimethyl-2-phenylethyl acetate in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²) applied under occlusion to the forearms/back of 25 patients; five alternate-day 48 h induction periods; 10 day rest; 48 h challenge occlusion; no SLS pretreatment
evidence.support_text: In human maximization tests with 4% 1,1-dimethyl-2-phenylethyl acetate in petrolatum on 25 patients, there was no reaction in any of the patients (RIFM, 1970, 1971c).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2-butanol in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²); 24-h occlusive pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate; five alternate-day 48-h occlusive applications; 10-day rest; challenge with 48-h occlusion preceded by 1-hour 10% sodium lauryl sulfate occlusion
evidence.support_text: Human maximization tests according to Kligman (1966) and Kligman and Epstein (1975) were carried out with 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2-butanol in petrolatum on a panel of 25 volunteers. There was no evidence of contact sensitization to 4% 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2-butanol in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²). After 24-h occlusive treatment on the patch sites with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate, 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2-butanol was applied under occlusion to the forearms of the volunteers for a total of five alternate-day 48-h periods. Following a 10-day rest period, challenge patches were applied under occlusion to fresh sites for 48 h. Challenge applications were preceded by one-hour applications of 10% sodium lauryl sulfate under occlusion. Challenge sites were evaluated at removal of the patches and 24 h later (RIFM 1973b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% hexadecanolide in petrolatum; application under occlusion to the same site on forearms/backs of 25 subjects for five alternate 48‑hour periods; sites pre‑treated for 24 hours with 5% aqueous SLS; challenge patches applied after 10–14 days for 48 hours
evidence.support_text: A 4% concentration of hexadecanolide in petrolatum did not elicit any sensitization reactions in 25 subjects in a human maximization test (RIFM, 1974b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% in petrolatum, occluded, 5 alternate day 48h induction patches on forearms with 24h pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS, 10-14 day rest, then 48h occluded challenge on fresh site
evidence.support_text: A maximization study according to Kligman (1966) and Kligman and Epstein (1975) was negative with a solution of 4% cycloheptadeca-9-en-1-one in petrolatum on 25 volunteers. Applications were occluded and made to the same site on the forearms for five alternate days, 48 h periods. Patch sites were pretreated with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate for 24 h. A challenge patch, under occlusion, was applied to a fresh site for 48 h after a 10–14 day rest period. There were no effects noted (RIFM, 1974b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% nerol in petrolatum, occlusive patches on forearms, five alternate-day 48-hour induction periods, SLS pretreatment, 10-day rest, 48-hour challenge with SLS pretreatment, 25 healthy male volunteers
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test (Kligman, 1966; Kligman and Epstein, 1975), 4% nerol in petrolatum was applied under occlusion to the forearms of 25 healthy male volunteers for five alternate-day 48-hour periods with SLS pretreatment. After a 10-day rest, a 48-hour challenge patch was applied to a fresh site with SLS pretreatment. No sensitization reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% nerolidol (2760 µg/cm²) in petrolatum; induction: five alternate-day 48-hour occlusive applications to forearms with 24-hour pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS); challenge: 48-hour occlusive patch to a fresh site with 10% aqueous SLS pretreatment; reading at patch removal and 24 h after removal; 25 healthy male volunteers.
evidence.support_text: A maximization test with 4% nerolidol in petrolatum on 25 healthy male volunteers, using occlusion and SLS pretreatment, found no sensitization reactions at challenge patch reading.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% p-isopropylbenzyl alcohol in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²) applied to 24 healthy male volunteers; five alternate-day 48h occlusive applications on forearms, each preceded by 24h treatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate; 10-14 day rest; challenge patches applied to scapular back under occlusion for 48h, preceded by 1h application of 10% sodium lauryl sulfate on left side; evaluated at removal and 24h later
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization test with 24 volunteers, 4% p-isopropylbenzyl alcohol in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²) showed no evidence of contact sensitization, despite sodium lauryl sulfate sites producing a large number of burned-appearing skin. The test material was applied under occlusion to the forearms for five alternate-day 48h periods, each preceded by 24h occlusive treatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate. After a 10-14 day rest, challenge patches were applied to fresh scapular back sites under occlusion for 48h, with challenge preceded by 1h of 10% sodium lauryl sulfate on the left side; sites were evaluated at patch removal and 24h later.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 6% (4140 µg/cm²) phenethyl formate in petrolatum, occlusive application to forearms for five alternate-day 48 h periods after 24 h pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS; 10-day rest; challenge patch on back for 48 h after 1 h pretreatment with 10% SLS; evaluated at 48 and 72 h.
evidence.support_text: A maximization test was carried out with 6% (4140 µg/cm²) phenethyl formate in petrolatum on 25 healthy male patients. Application was under occlusion for five-alternate day 48 h periods with SLS pretreatment. After a 10 day rest, challenge patches were applied to fresh sites on the back for 48 h under occlusion with SLS pretreatment. No sensitization reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 6% beta-methylphenethyl alcohol in petrolatum (4140 µg/cm²); occlusion; forearms or backs; SLS pretreatment (5% aqueous SLS under occlusion for 24 hours); induction: 5 alternate-day 48-hour periods; 10–14 day rest; challenge under occlusion for 48 hours after SLS pretreatment; reactions read at patch removal and 24 hours later.
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization study, there was no sensitization reactions to 6% β-methylphenethyl alcohol in petrolatum in any of the 25 subjects tested (4140 µg/cm²) (RIFM, 1974b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 6% phenyl salicylate in petrolatum, occlusion, 25 healthy volunteers (male and female), induction for five alternate day 48-hour periods with 24-hour pretreatment of 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate under occlusion, challenge patch with 6% phenyl salicylate in petrolatum, readings on patch removal and 24 h later.
evidence.support_text: A human maximization test was conducted with 6% phenyl salicylate in petrolatum under occlusion on the volar forearms of 25 healthy male and female volunteers for five alternate day 48-hour periods, with patch sites pretreated for 24 h with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate under occlusion. After a rest period, a challenge patch with 6% phenyl salicylate in petrolatum was applied; readings were taken on patch removal and 24 h later. No sensitization reactions were observed (RIFM, 1975a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8% cedrol (5520 µg/cm²) in petrolatum, occlusion, induction: 5 alternate-day 48-hour periods with 24h pretreatment of 5% aqueous SLS, challenge after 10-day rest: 48h occlusion with 1h pretreatment of 10% aqueous SLS

evidence.support_text: When the maximization test was repeated using the same method and cedrol concentration (8% in petrolatum), no sensitization reactions were observed in 25 volunteers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8% in petrolatum, 5520 µg/cm², occlusion on forearms or backs, pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS for 24h under occlusion, five alternate-day 48h induction periods, 10-day rest, challenge patch 48h under occlusion preceded by 60 min SLS, reading at patch removal and 72h
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization study involving 25 subjects, there were no positive reactions to 8% α-methylbenzyl alcohol in petrolatum (5520 µg/cm²) (RIFM, 1973b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8% isojasmone in petrolatum (5520 µg/cm²), induction phase: 24-h pretreatment with 5% sodium lauryl sulfate followed by five alternate-day 48-h occluded applications on forearm; challenge concentration 8% (5520 µg/cm²), scored upon removal and 24 h later
evidence.support_text: In a human maximization study, 25 volunteers received induction with 8% isojasmone in petrolatum (5520 µg/cm²) under occlusion following SLS pretreatment. Challenge with the same concentration produced no reactions in any subject.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.1% PPD in petrolatum (71.4 µg/cm²), 1 ml/14 cm² under occlusion (Werbril patch) for 48 h, pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS for 24 h. Elicitation: PPD in petrolatum, 0.4 ml/2.54 cm² under occlusion for 48 h; reading at removal and 48 h later.
evidence.support_text: In the Human Maximization Test, PPD at an induction dose of 0.1% (71.4 µg/cm²) gave 5/24 positive reactions (20%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 1 ml of 8% cis-jasmone in petrolatum (5520 µg/cm²) under occlusion for 5 alternate-day 48-h periods to forearm, first induction preceded by 24 h treatment with 5% sodium lauryl sulfate; challenge: 8% cis-jasmone in petrolatum under occlusion for 48 h to back, preceded by 30 min application of 5% sodium lauryl sulfate; scoring upon removal and 24 h later
evidence.support_text: In a maximization study, 1 ml of 8% cis-jasmone in petrolatum was applied under occlusion for 5 alternate-day 48-h periods to the forearm of 25 adult male volunteers, with the first induction preceded by 24 h treatment with 5% sodium lauryl sulfate. Following a 10-14 day rest, a challenge dose of 8% cis-jasmone in petrolatum was applied under occlusion for 48 h to the back, preceded by 30 min application of 5% sodium lauryl sulfate. evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test using 30 female albino Dunkin Hartley guinea pigs, intradermal induction with 1% vol/vol Glyceryl Thioglycolate in distilled water and topical induction with 10% vol/vol, followed by topical challenge with 10% vol/vol, a sensitization rate of 56% was observed based on erythema/edema reactions at the challenge sites (9 of 16 treated animals showed very slight to well-defined erythema within 24 hours).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female Hartley guinea pigs, 5 per group. evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test by Katsuno et al. evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, Magnusson and Kligman method; induction: 10% intradermal with and without FCA, followed by 48-h occluded patch at 25% after 6-8 days; challenge: occluded patch at 10% and 3% for 24h; readings at 24 and 48h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: In a Guinea pig maximization test with 10% intradermal and 25% topical induction doses, methyl 2,6,10-trimethylcyclododeca-2,5,9-trien-1-yl ketone caused barely perceptible erythema in 2/10 males at 10% challenge but no reactions at 3% challenge or in females, leading to the conclusion that the compound was a weak sensitizer (RIFM, 1987a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, Magnusson and Kligman method; induction: 2% intradermal with and without FCA, followed by 48-h occluded patch at 100% after 6-8 days; challenges: occluded patch at 50% and 5% for 24h; three challenge rounds at intervals of one week or more; readings at 24 and 48h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: In a Guinea pig maximization test with 2% intradermal and 100% topical induction doses, methyl 2,6,10-trimethylcyclododeca-2,5,9-trien-1-yl ketone produced positive reactions in multiple challenges, with up to 6/20 animals showing reactions at 48h, and the study concluded the compound was a weak sensitizer (RIFM, 1988b).
